subject: Peering handshake, streaming concurrency & KV-cache plan for private deployment
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Chen <sam.chen@dataflow.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jun 2028 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Peering handshake, streaming concurrency & KV-cache plan for private deployment

Sam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before the lab: 

Summary (what we agreed)
- Target tail latency goals for streaming inference (model: open-8b-q): 95th <= 120 ms, 99th <= 220 ms for token-emission latency once KV-cache warmed.
- Concurrency: initial qualification target = 250 sustained concurrent streaming sessions; scale target = 500 for peak planning.
- Non-streaming throughput (short responses / reranking): baseline 1,200 QPS (95th token latency budget <= 180 ms).
- Networking expectations: direct peering/VPN between your on-prem border and our private peering endpoints; egress IPs, MTU, and NAT behavior will be validated in lab.

Immediate asks for your network team before the lab:
1) Provide a short list of site egress IPs (CSV) and the public ASN or FW appliance vendor + model.
2) Share an internal contact for L3 (we have Peter listed; please confirm).
3) If possible, run a quick iperf3 between your edge and our public peering test IPs (we'll supply endpoints) to check throughput and MTU.

Attachments: SLO template and a lightweight network checklist (attached). (Attachment: slo-matrix-template.xlsx, spreadsheet) (Attachment: network-checklist.md, text)

Proposed lab (2-hour remote session) — goals and tests:
- Connectivity: confirm UDP/TCP egress, NAT behavior, MTU, and path MTU discovery.
- Bandwidth/throughput: sustained iperf3 at target concurrency profiles (50/150/250 streams).
- Streaming tail-latency capture: short-run (5–10 min) streaming sessions with token-per-second profiling + KV-cache warmup routine to observe improvement slope.
- Acceptance criteria: 95th <= 120 ms and 99th <= 220 ms after KV warm; packet loss <= 0.1%; sustained throughput >= 80% of link.

Proposed timeslot: Jun 17, 10:00–12:00 PT. If that works we'll share ephemeral test endpoints and a step-by-step runbook.

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben and Karthik on the lab prep.

— Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@dataflow.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Liu <peter.liu@dataflow.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jun 2028 09:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Peering handshake, streaming concurrency & KV-cache plan for private deployment

Irene — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers from our side and a couple of follow-ups: 

- Site egress IPs: attached (site-egress-ips.csv). We exit through a pair of Palo Alto FWs (PA-5220) into a single public IP NAT.
- L3/NetOps contact: Peter Liu (copied) will own the firewall/peering config.
- Existing measurements: our internal tests to one of Redwood's public edges (us-west) show ~42–55 ms RTT; we haven't tested your private peering endpoints yet.

Questions:
1) For KV-cache warmup, can you share the pattern generator script or a short example of the prefix sequences you recommend?
2) For the streaming sessions, is TLS termination expected on our side or do you prefer mutual-TLS to the Redwood edge?

We can do the Jun 17 slot — please send the endpoints and any pre-lab checklist. We'll attach a short PCAP capture from a previous test for reference (pcap-sample.pcap).

Thanks,
Sam Chen
Senior Platform Engineer, DataFlow AI
sam.chen@dataflow.ai | +1 (650) 555-4210
(Attachment: site-egress-ips.csv, csv) (Attachment: pcap-sample.pcap, pcap)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Chen <sam.chen@dataflow.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jun 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Peering handshake, streaming concurrency & KV-cache plan for private deployment

Sam — great, thanks for the egress file and the pcap. Answers inline and a short pre-lab plan: 

1) KV-cache warmup: attached is a tiny generator (example snippets below). Plan is to prefill prefixes of 8–64 tokens for 10K unique keys to approximate warm steady-state before measuring tail latency. We’ll hand you the script and a seed list during the lab.

2) TLS: we support both. For fastest setup, terminate TLS at your edge and TCP forward to our peering IPs. If you need mTLS for compliance, we can provide client certs and an ephemeral PKI for the lab. Please indicate preference in your pre-lab ticket.

Pre-lab checklist (we will provide a runbook as well):
- Open outbound 443 to Redwood peering test IPs (we’ll share).
- Allow ICMP (for traceroute/MTU tests) from our test IPs.
- Temporary low-timeout NAT mapping (we prefer 30s) to avoid early TCP tears during long streaming sessions.
- Upload your sample PCAP and egress IPs into the shared Drive folder (link below).

Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Streaming: 95th <= 120 ms; 99th <= 220 ms after KV warm (250 concurrent streams).
- Non-streaming throughput: 1,200 QPS with 95th <= 180 ms.
- Network: packet loss <= 0.1% end-to-end; RTT < 120 ms to peering IP.

We’ll provide ephemeral test endpoints and an instrumentation header (x-rd-request-id) to correlate traces. Proposed slot still Jun 17, 10:00–12:00 PT — please confirm.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example

— Irene
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jun 2028 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Peering handshake, streaming concurrency & KV-cache plan for private deployment

Irene / Ben — a few ops notes for the runbook and what we’ll provision from the Redwood side: 

- Test endpoints: we will spin up two ephemeral peering endpoints in us-west with public peering IPs and a dedicated ingress route for DF-3742. Endpoints available ~1 hour before the test.
- Certs: if DF wants mTLS, we can issue short-lived client certs (valid 24 hours). Default is TLS to your edge.
- Concurrency guidance: our runtime has been validated up to ~600 concurrent streaming sessions per GPU in lab environments, but real-world pod sizing and KV-cache effects mean we recommend starting at 250 per pod and scaling horizontally. For the lab we’ll do the 50/150/250 ramp profile.
- Instrumentation: we’ll require x-rd-request-id and x-rd-kv-warm headers to correlate cold vs warm token emissions. We’ll also push per-route tracing to your S3/Drive bucket for post-test analysis.
- Runbook snippets: iperf3 legacy (tcp) and iperf3 --udp for loss characterization; use tcpreplay against pcap to reproduce conditions if needed.

I’ll attach a short checklist to the runbook with exact commands and expected outputs.

— Karthik
Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@dataflow.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Peering handshake, streaming concurrency & KV-cache plan for private deployment

All — confirmed for Jun 17, 10:00–12:00 PT. I’ve uploaded the pcap and egress CSV to the Drive folder and submitted a Firewall change request for outbound to the peering IP range (ETA approval: ~6 hours).

Files attached here for the thread: site-egress-ips.csv, pcap-sample.pcap. We’ll prefer TLS termination at our edge for this initial run; if you can provide ephemeral client certs we’ll stand up mTLS in a follow-up test.

Procurement/Docusign note: our vendor team needs a draft SOW to expedite procurement — I’ll drop the DocuSign link once internal approvals are in. For now we have the lab approvals.

Thanks — looking forward to the test.

— Sam
